messages.author: 97d82fedb7016adb
messages.subject: warmup seems broken in develop
parts:
Hi there!

I was running a ~1.5 month old cmdstan snapshot without a problem. I thought updating to the current version in develop would be a good idea. I also set stan and stan-math to the most recent develop versions (cmdstan refers to older git submodules).

Now my models only give me crap! That is, most of the runs are incredibly fast, only few runs run at a normal speed. To me it looks as if warmup fails to do something sensible (my residual error is way too large). I have to say that some chains give me results which are ok (different seed and different chain_id).

To cross check I also checked out cmdstan with the snapshot versions as the git submodules are set currently, see below for the hashes.

Model and data can't be shared, sorry; but I am happy to try out any updates on them.

Best,
Sebastian

cmdstan submodules:
[weberse2@node13:~/libs/cmdstan] make stan-update
git submodule update --init --recursive
Submodule path 'stan': checked out 'fb1b76962cd8495812c87f0a0e0d8ab328444f34'
Submodule path 'stan/lib/stan_math': checked out 'fe69fed0c91ac1c9f022673d70d7d94c48296e38'

messages.author: 97d82fedb7016adb
messages.subject: Re: warmup seems broken in develop
parts:
Doing a bit more testing reveals that the cmdstan hashes

- 169c0fb does not work; 17 April
- 27e078f WORKS OK (before the BIG HMC refactor); 26 March

So something between the above two cmdstan hashes makes the warmup fail - at least on my model. We need some test for this, but I have no clue yet where to start.

Sebastian

Yep, I hope this is helpful. My guess is that this has to do with changes in stan which happened between those commits. In particular, those changes done to the HMC sub-system. From my impression so far, the bug seems to be triggered more reliably the more random effects you have.

I hope someone can create a minimal example which we can throw into a test - I don't have one ready yet, but from my perspective this should (in fact must) be adressed before we tag 2.10.

Sebastian
